"issue-138" (2026-10-05T21:07:23Z) — 6 section(s):

[1] "issue-138" section 1:
Issue #138 in re-cinq/Otto: Answer a tool call whose executor threw instead of failing the turn
State: closed
Author: gedaiu
Labels: size:S, type:feature, area:tools, repo:hal-engine, epic:E2
Opened: 2026-08-21T09:39:04Z
Closed: 2026-10-05T21:07:22Z
Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/Otto/issues/138

Part of #56

## Why

`ToolRegistry.execute` awaits the registered executor with no `try`, so whatever it throws rejects one of the promises in `executeToolCalls`'s `Promise.all`, escapes `processMessageStream`, and becomes a `SERVER_ERROR` / "Failed to process message" that ends the customer's whole conversation - taking every other tool result from the same round with it. The docs already tell tool authors not to throw, but nothing enforces it. `079` drew the line for every model-caused failure; this issue closes the last gap, an executor's own defect.

[2] "issue-138" section 2:
## What to do

Wrap the executor call and `normalizeToolResponse` in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts:83-92` in a `try/catch`. On catch, log the tool name, `error.name` and the message (truncated to 500 characters, matching the org's existing bound in `cfoagent`'s `gemini.ts`) at `error` level, and return a resolved `ToolResponse` whose `result` is a fixed English sentence naming the tool - never the thrown message itself, since a third-party error string can carry an internal hostname or another customer's identifier and the engine redacts nothing. Handle non-`Error` throws (`throw 'boom'`, `throw undefined`) the same way. Leave `onError` un-fired for a caught throw - the turn now succeeds, so no failure hook runs - and update `docs/tool-responses.md`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to describe the backstop. The one remaining throw path is `Object.keys(input)` rejecting on a `null` input from a malformed caller - that's a caller bug, stays outside the `try`, and gets a JSDoc `@throws`.

[3] "issue-138" section 3:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `execute('get_weather', {})` against an executor that rejects with `new Error('ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.4:8080')` resolves rather than rejects, returning `toEqual({result: <string>})` with no `clientMessages` and no `suppressAssistantResponse`
- [ ] The returned `result` contains `get_weather` and contains neither `ECONNREFUSED` nor `10.0.0.4`
- [ ] A table-driven test covers `throw 'boom'`, `throw undefined` and `throw {code: 500}`, and all three produce a resolved `ToolResponse` of the same shape as the `Error` case
- [ ] `log.error` is called exactly once per crashed call with topic `tool`, the tool name and `error.name`; a 2000-character error message is logged truncated to 500 characters
- [ ] A throwing executor called with `{booking_id: 'B-1', customer_name: 'Ada Example'}` produces no returned text and no log line containing `B-1` or `Ada`
- [ ] A round with one throwing executor and one working executor returns **both** results: the working executor's `result` reaches `messages` unchanged

[4] "issue-138" section 4:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An end-to-end `chatOrchestrator` test with a throwing executor asserts `processMessage` resolves and the provider's second call receives a `tool_result` block naming the tool
- [ ] The same test asserts `onError` was **not** called while `afterModelResponse` **was** - the turn succeeded
- [ ] `execute` carries JSDoc stating the three-part contract: resolves for a model-caused failure, resolves for an executor throw, throws only for caller-malformed input
- [ ] `docs/tool-responses.md`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md` and `docs/architecture.md` state that a throwing executor is caught, the model is told the call failed, and the thrown message reaches only the log
- [ ] `.specify/spec.md` records that the backstop is what makes the tool-result invariant hold for a crashing executor, and that the `error` log line is the only source for the "Tool Success Rate" metric it already claims
- [ ] The PR body records the breaking-change note: `execute` no longer rejects on an executor throw, the bump is MINOR, and no code outside `hal-engine` calls `execute` directly today

[5] "issue-138" section 5:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **NIS-2 Article 21 operational resilience.** A test asserts the customer-visible outcome of a crashing tool is a completed turn (`sendStreamEnd` reached), not `SERVER_ERROR`
- [ ] **GDPR.** The spec states the thrown message is bounded and logged but never redacted, that the engine cannot enforce what a tool author puts in an error string, and that `003-support-conversation-data-flow-record` gains a row for the tool-error log line
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the changed public surface

[6] "issue-138" section 6:
## Tech notes

This is a deliberate departure from `cfoagent`'s pattern of forwarding the raw error string to the model (`gemini.ts:938-970`) - that code's tools call one internal system whose error strings the same team writes, which doesn't hold for a registry any consumer can register into. Placement follows `079` rather than the orchestrator: `execute` is the published seam, and two docs reproduce its `Promise.all` snippet directly, so a fix that only holds inside the orchestrator wouldn't hold for them. No new hook is added for observing a crashed tool - a consumer wraps its own executor at registration if it needs one, which `048`'s `registerTools.ts` already does.

Out of scope: telling the provider a result is an error on the wire (`130` owns that), the tool entry already shown on the customer's screen for a call that failed (queued separately), a per-call deadline (`090`), and the `onError` `instanceof Error` guard measured in `036` (widening it changes what a *provider* failure does, a different question).

Build with `/lore-feature "Answer a tool call whose executor threw instead of failing the turn"` - spec lands at `specs/hal-engine-tool-executor-throw/spec.md`, tasks at `tasks.md`, description via `/lore-pr`.
